summary: Removes the npm package manager from the production backend image after its Chainguard package was renamed, and upgrades the transitive Nano ID dependency to a patched release.
userImpact: The backend runtime image no longer reports the eight high and medium findings tracked by GitHub issue #350.
The security remediation adds no API, configuration, or schema changes beyond those documented for the access-governance release.

instructions: Upgrade and redeploy the EnterpriseGlue 0.11.0 backend image.
Verify the deployed image digest and rerun the container vulnerability scan.

notes: The security remediation adds no database changes beyond the 0.11.0 authorization, identity, and engine-governance migration series.

security: Removes versioned Alpine/Wolfi npm packages such as npm-12 from the final backend image instead of matching only the historical npm package name.
Upgrades PostCSS to resolve Nano ID 3.3.17 or newer and eliminate CVE-2026-67213.
Extends the published-image runtime contract to reject npm and versioned npm package names.
documentation: GitHub security drift issue #350 documents the original findings and affected published image.
rollback: Redeploy the previous backend image only if operational rollback is required; doing so reintroduces the reported vulnerabilities.
validation: Build the production backend image for AMD64 and ARM64 and verify npm executables, directories, and package database entries are absent.
Scan both production image architectures for medium, high, and critical vulnerabilities and confirm issue #350 findings are absent.
Run the access-governance, contract-parity, application, image, and release-note gates for the 0.11.0 draft.
